results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Audited all 127 aligned units, p01–p127, against the independent summaries in draft order. The summaries recover the distinction, material analogy, planning consequences, operating loop, evidence and stable-core requirements, application, and synthesis; table-bearing units p11, p19, p35, p42, p59, p65, and p80 match when their attached comparisons are included. The opening callout is correctly unmapped evidence rather than an extra spec paragraph.

Audited the callout and every prose/list unit p01–p127; the independent outliner flagged no unit as having two controlling ideas. Longer units such as p02 and the example lists p25, p45, p53, p62, p69, p86, and p120 develop one governing claim, process, inventory, or diagnostic purpose through several related dimensions.

Every unit p01–p127 and the opening callout contributes to S1–S5: p01–p29 establish the AI distinction and changing material (S1/S2); p30–p46 derive planning and management consequences (S2/S4/S5); p47–p60 explain selective change (S4/S5); p61–p82 establish evaluation and customer evidence (S2/S3/S5); p83–p88 establish continuity (S4); p89–p120 apply those commitments (S2–S5); p121–p127 synthesize them and locate human responsibility. The reference apparatus supports optional further reading rather than opening a competing argument.

Audited all 77 spec evidence items (47 reasoning items, two attributed sources, seven tables, four figures, 14 examples, and three analogies), all actual tables/figure captions, the opening callout, and quoted statements in the draft. The two-AI comparison leads to the false-progress inference; planning and management tables lead to stable-versus-changeable choices and the editor role; the fad comparison leads to judgment; evaluation layers and Figure 4 establish worth beyond a demo; the model/product table leads to customer observation. Conditional media examples, regressions, anti-patterns, and analogies state their consequence in their own unit or its immediate continuation. The Beek anecdote explains the metaphor’s origin and Holmquist supplies the design-material framing; this checks their argumentative use, not independent factual verification.

Audited all 127 declared transitions: 111 paragraph transitions, including the opening incoming bridge, and 16 section/conclusion transitions; these cover every adjacent in-draft unit boundary. Actual text conveys the declared contrasts, elaborations, examples, consequences, sequences, and syntheses. Representative bridges include “Those changing assumptions also affect how long a plan can remain useful” at p30, “Those product-management extensions and the seasonal product brief” at p47, the release-decision framing at p98, and “The questions return us to the distinction” at p121. Repeated “Teams need” paragraphs and the labeled principles/anti-patterns retain a clear shared subject while introducing each declared next dimension.

Both independent flow readers recover the whole progression from distinction and material changes through operating model, safeguards, and application, matching the post’s problem–solution order and the section comparison, prerequisite, process, and grouping patterns. Each reader accounts for all 15 body sections, the conclusion, and the optional references. Both explicitly report no lost thread or need for reordering; their observations about repetition concern pace, and both distinguish the jobs performed by the repeated material.

Audited first uses and paragraph openings across the callout and p01–p127 using the engineering-leader context stated in the introduction bridge. AI-assisted delivery and AI-powered customer value are explicitly contrasted; unit economics and latency receive immediate glosses; modalities receive examples; golden workflow is explained at its first substantive use before golden scenarios recur; the fashion mapping establishes collection, silhouette, fit, and archive before the operating loop reuses them. Capability substrate is immediately restated as the underlying models. Neither independent flow reader identifies an unexplained term or missing prerequisite.

The callout and Introduction p01–p10 pose a specific product decision, state the proposed answer, explain the AI distinction, ground the metaphor in a practitioner anecdote, and announce the route. The opening is neither a placeholder nor a merely restated question, dictionary opening, sweeping historical preamble, or book report.

The Real Shift p121–p127 returns to the initial distinction, joins changing material with evaluation and a stable promise, explains the scarcity of value judgment, and gives an action. It neither withholds the thesis until the close nor ends with repetition alone, sentiment, or unrelated evidence. Its leadership hand-off extends the human judgment already developed at p88 and p108 rather than adding an unsupported new argument.

Across p121–p127, the close connects the separate mechanisms established by the material, evaluation, and stable-core sections: evaluation lets a durable customer promise survive changing implementation by testing each change as a customer-value bet. P125 explains why that connection matters when rebuilding becomes cheaper, and p126 converts it into preservation and release decisions.
results.quote: Above all, **evaluation matters**: it lets a stable customer promise survive a changing implementation by testing each change as a customer-value bet.

results.finding: P121 explicitly returns to faster delivery versus changed product value, the distinction posed by the introductory model-release question. P122 and p126 then answer the product side with an evaluation discipline and preserved user jobs, fulfilling the declared callback.
results.quote: The questions return us to the distinction between faster delivery and changed product value.

results.finding: The introduction-only reader predicts the complete announced sequence: delivery/product distinction; fashion, materials, seasons, and modern product management; seasonal rhythm versus fad chasing; evaluation, customer evidence, and stable promise; then routines, principles, anti-patterns, and application questions. Its expectation of practical comparisons and examples, rather than quantitative research, matches the body’s seven tables, four explanatory figures, conditional examples, and practitioner tone. No substantive prediction is unmet.

The AC-1 cold reader distinguishes AI used in delivery from AI supplying customer-facing capability, explains changed workflows, interfaces, expectations, costs and failure behavior, and identifies preservation/rebuilding decisions. The answer retains engineering review and outcome/customer/business evidence while adding repeated reconsideration of model assumptions and product fit, satisfying the expected distinction and extension.

results.finding: The AC-2 cold reader explains that benchmark gains can regress representative jobs, expert control, consistency, tone, safety/privacy, latency, cost, or the product promise, and that adoption and commercial value require customer evidence. It also names comparisons and stopping criteria; its refusal to decide a specific unmeasured migration is consistent with the article’s scope.

results.finding: The AC-3 cold reader reconstructs scouting, an explicit value/promise/stop-condition brief, preservation of existing jobs and trust, comparison of old and new on representative and customer/business evidence, exploratory testing before commitment, selective ship/delay/retire/revert decisions, and archived learning. The distinction between exploration and commitment is explicit; noting the absence of universal thresholds accurately respects the product-specific decision framework.
